_comment: Provenance for everything under vendors/. Managed by scripts/vendor_retroarch.py.
Both RetroArch builds are gitignored and fetched on demand: 193 MiB for
Windows and 171 MiB for Linux. Neither belongs in git history, which every
clone on every platform pays for.
Both are also directory trees rather than single files -- RetroArch dlopens
its cores and resolves libGL and the host's audio stack from the host, so
no platform gets a single portable binary. 'sha256' pins the download and
'tree_sha256' pins what unpacking it produced, which is what actually
ships and is the only one --verify can still check once the download cache
libretro publishes no checksums, so a null hash is filled in on first fetch
(trust on first use). Review and commit the recorded hashes: from then on any
drift in the upstream file is a hard failure instead of a silent swap.
RetroArch's own licence text is not inside any of these artifacts -- the
Windows archive carries only assets/COPYING (CC-BY-4.0, for the assets).
GPLv3 redistribution requires shipping it, so vendors/RetroArch-COPYING is
committed here, taken from the upstream tag the binary was built from.

win64.description: RetroArch portable build for Windows x86_64

linux-x86_64.description: RetroArch portable build for Linux x86_64
_note: The archive holds an AppImage plus a 390 MiB .home tree of assets and
shaders; only the AppImage is extracted, and it is then unwrapped into
the portable tree it already contains (issue #328). Same upstream
bytes, no FUSE, no unpacking at launch.
libretro publishes no ARM build -- stable/<version>/linux/ lists x86
and x86_64 and nothing else -- so there is no linux-aarch64 entry here
and the ARM packages use the distribution's RetroArch (issue #119).

retroarch_licence.description: RetroArch's own licence text, shipped beside every vendored binary
_note: Committed rather than fetched at build time: the build already has one
network dependency too many, and a licence that has to download is a
licence that can be missing from a release. Refresh it when the
vendored RetroArch version changes, from that version's own tag.
